rule.description: A function or method reaches directly into public instance data owned by a class of this project through an object received as a parameter (or a simple alias of one), instead of asking that object's class to do the work. Attribute accesses used as call functions (delegation) do not count. Reported when one parameter carries at least 3 distinct public attributes, at least 3 total accesses, and more accesses than the function performs on its own object. Attribute sets are anchored to classes defined in this repository (public instance attributes assigned to self in __init__, including project base-class inheritance).
rule.exit_contract: 0 when no envious reach into project-owned state is found; non-zero when the smell is present, required source is missing/unparsable, or the analysis cannot complete reliably

checks.description: Detect functions and methods that work directly on the public instance data of a project class they received as a parameter, rather than delegating to that class's own behavior.
checks.detected_relation: function/method -> public instance data owned by a project class, reached through a parameter or a simple local alias of one
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Behavior derived from a class's data (reading its response indicators, consulting per-worker counters, updating progress accounting) lives outside the class that owns and initializes that data, so the owner can no longer evolve those data usages or their invariants in one place. Attribute accesses used as the function part of a call are not counted: delegation is the shape the rule wants to see, this rule flags data reaches.

excluded.what: Reaches into module namespaces and third-party objects
excluded.why_not_this_rule: Ownership must be a decision this codebase can make. Module namespaces (os, sys, time, random, ...) and third-party library objects (pycurl, paramiko, dnslib, ajpylib, http.server parser machinery, ...) cannot have behavior moved into them from this repository, so attribute accesses on them are not feature envy here. The rule anchors only on classes defined in this repository.
excluded.examples: producer/consumer functions indexing os.environ; TCP classes accumulating pycurl handle attributes; dns_query working on dnslib records

excluded.why_not_this_rule: An attribute used as the function part of a call (obj.method()) is the exact shape the rule wants to encourage, not a data reach, so those accesses are not counted.

Isolated one- or two-attribute reads through a parameter are ordinary collaboration, not misplaced behavior; the rule requires at least 3 distinct public attributes, at least 3 total accesses, and more accesses on that parameter than on the function's own object.
excluded.examples: log_result(...) consulting resp.code once; helpers receiving a Progress instance for a single flip of done_count
